zh: 旅遊埃及時，觀賞了許多神廟古殿遺跡，体驗古埃及宏偉精巧的文明形態和內涵。參觀 Aswan 附近 Kom Ombo神廟時，正值黃昏時分，落日餘輝灑落在殘垣斷柱上，                              飄放出迥光返照的柔麗蒼涼。見老者枯坐廟前，神情茫然，隱約有 "千年歲月留崢嶸，十載生涯歸寂寞" 的古今對比。低迴流連，不禁懷想起時空之外，南投竹山近郊的德山寺。
en: While traveling in Egypt, I viewed many ancient temples and palace ruins, experiencing the grand and intricate form and substance of ancient Egyptian civilization. When visiting the Kom Ombo Temple near Aswan, it happened to be dusk, and the glow of the setting sun scattered across the broken pillars and ruined walls, casting off a soft, desolate afterglow like the last gleam before darkness. I saw an old man sitting withered before the temple, his expression distant, faintly evoking the ancient-and-modern contrast of 'a thousand years of glory left behind, ten years of life returning to solitude.' Lingering there, reluctant to leave, I could not help but recall, beyond time and space, Deshan Temple near Zhushan in Nantou.
If there were an ancient temple
When I am covered in dust and dew
Returning from a thousand miles away
The stone clean, the rain stopped
Leaves full of cicada song
One can break a willow branch and chase the wind
One can touch the wall and watch the stars
perhaps,
A hidden fragrance drifts all around
Trees mirrored in the pond
Moss mottled and worn
The water's color, blurred and faint
Butterfly shadows flit through the morning fog
In the dusk, frog song slowly rises
perhaps,
Along the flower path, water flows with a tinkling sound
In the deep shade, a bell tolls, slow and lingering
Listening to the wooden drum's Sanskrit chant
Letting the ancient melody
Petal by petal, peeling away
How much
The mood of an old road under the slanting sun
perhaps,
Passing through stone steps scattered with falling leaves
Over the rice fields the sky lies still
Wild geese fly south, returning
Evening clouds hang low
Watching the reeds along the riverbank
How to stir the flowing light's reflection
How to recall the hazy years
If there were an ancient temple
When I am covered in dust and dew
Returning from a thousand miles away
The moon faint, clouds sparse
The forest quiet, still as Zen
Tree shadows sway in the courtyard
Inside the window, a lone lamp dims
Brushed past by the evening wind
Apricot blossoms, bamboo shadows
Asking what evening this evening is

points.zh:
Kom Ombo 位於 Aswan 南方約三十公里處, 是尼羅河畔的古城。Kom 的意思是金，Ombo是山，Kom Ombo就是「金山」的意思。是古埃及黄金之都的舊址，古埃及的宫庭金品, 陪葬物，棺材等金飾都是來自此處。尼羅河在此轉灣處，兇猛鱷魚横行，當時埃及人把鱷魚當神供奉。
Kom Ombo 神廟大約建於西元前180～145年間，經歷代君王加蓋擴建而成。在漫長歲月中，因尼羅河汜濫，地震，以及侵佔掠奪, 神廟淪成廢墟。直到十九世紀末期才開始修築復建。Kom Ombo神廟是埃及唯一的雙神神廟 ( double temple ) ，南殿供奉鱷魚神Sobek，北殿供奉老鷹神Horus，神廟建築的特色是以一個中軸爲主，分隔完全對稱的南北兩殿，兩個入口，兩個中庭，兩個廊柱廳，兩座内墊祭壇。其牆壁石柱浮雕精美，人物裝飾栩栩生動，還有太陽月曆，醫學手術儀器和產婦坐姿等圖像。神廟内的鱷魚博物館有多尊鱷魚木乃伊。
points.en:
Kom Ombo is located about thirty kilometers south of Aswan, an ancient city on the banks of the Nile. 'Kom' means gold and 'Ombo' means mountain, so Kom Ombo means 'Gold Mountain.' It was the site of ancient Egypt's capital of gold, and the golden objects used in the royal court, burial goods, and coffins of ancient Egypt all came from here. Where the Nile bends at this point, fierce crocodiles were once common, and the ancient Egyptians worshipped the crocodile as a god.
The Temple of Kom Ombo was built around 180-145 BC and was expanded and added to by successive rulers over the generations. Over the long centuries, due to flooding of the Nile, earthquakes, and plundering, the temple fell into ruin. Restoration work did not begin until the late nineteenth century. The Temple of Kom Ombo is the only double temple in Egypt: the southern hall is dedicated to the crocodile god Sobek, and the northern hall to the falcon god Horus. The temple's architecture is built along a central axis, dividing it into two perfectly symmetrical halves, north and south, each with its own entrance, courtyard, hypostyle hall, and inner sanctuary altar. The relief carvings on its stone walls and columns are finely detailed, with lifelike figural decoration, and also include images such as a solar calendar, medical and surgical instruments, and a woman giving birth in a seated position. The crocodile museum inside the temple houses numerous crocodile mummies.

points.zh:
數年前回去台灣時，趁清晨曙光未現，和美智二弟驅車自台中南下，到南投竹山附近山腰，攝取薄霧迷朦的山嶺日出景象。 回程時造訪竹山西南郊的德山寺。德山寺，俗稱德山巖，大約創建於清朝乾隆年間，距今已近三百年。《 雲林縣采訪冊 》記載 : 「 德山巖在縣東南二十八里，依山環抱, 綠樹幽篁，映帶左右，泉聲鳥語，曲徑花香，四顧蒼茫，群峰聳翠，尤極眼界之奇觀。」德山寺的入口處有牌坊，其聯云: 「 德業愛何充，暮鼓晨鐘開覺路，山門來賈島，竹風松籟入詩篇 」。寺前闢有半月形池塘，池畔遍植山櫻，杜鵑，龍柏，楊柳等花木，近旁有孟中竹掩映。時值清明時節，姹紫嫣紅，綠影搖曳，映照水面。池後殿前，廣庭清靜，一片青綠如茵。殿左羅漢松下，有立石刻字，幽雅閒致。德山寺的環境，清幽怡人，飄散着淡雅閒逸的禪意，能消擾擾市井俗慮。登臨探望，竟覺八方勝景，都來一處。
離開德山寺，走的是一條寧靜柔美的田莊路。挿秧後的水田，倒映着雲光山色，華原茂野，滿眼翠綠。牛車走過的鄉村道路，恬靜的村莊，漫漫迤邐的山嶺，晨霧漸散 ..... ，舊時的農村情景不由地浮上眼前 : 夏日黃昏，莊稼漢光著上身，三五成群，坐在小店的板條凳上，村老叨著香煙閒聊於樹蔭下，田埂上荷鋤走向歸途的農夫，背着書包放學回家的孩童, 街頭偶而傳來幾聲狗吠 ......,  動人的畫面, 散放着安樂和祥的氛圍。「 遠山日落煙迷處，彷彿當年從此去，浦口村童放犢歸，停驂借問來時路。」清初女詩人林以寧的《山程》詩，迴映着當時的心情。
points.en:
A few years ago, returning to Taiwan, before dawn's first light my younger brother Meizhi and I drove south from Taichung to a hillside near Zhushan in Nantou, to capture the misty mountain sunrise. On the way back we visited Deshan Temple southwest of Zhushan. Deshan Temple, also known as Deshan Rock, was founded roughly during the Qianlong era of the Qing dynasty, nearly three hundred years ago. The Yunlin County Gazetteer records: "Deshan Rock lies twenty-eight li southeast of the county seat, embraced by mountains on all sides, with green trees and secluded bamboo groves reflecting each other, the sound of springs and birdsong, winding paths fragrant with flowers; looking all around, a vast expanse, with ranges of green peaks rising — truly a most extraordinary view." At the entrance to Deshan Temple stands a memorial archway, with a couplet reading: "How full is its virtuous work — the morning bell and evening drum open the path to enlightenment; to this mountain gate comes a Jia Dao — the sound of bamboo in the wind and pine mingles into verse." In front of the temple lies a crescent-shaped pond, its banks planted with mountain cherry, azalea, dragon juniper, and willow, with a grove of bamboo nearby casting its shade. It happened to be the Qingming season, and the vivid reds and purples, with rippling green shadows, were reflected on the water's surface. Behind the pond, before the main hall, lies a broad, quiet courtyard, all green as a carpet. Under the podocarpus trees to the left of the hall stands an inscribed stone, elegant and at ease. The surroundings of Deshan Temple are tranquil and pleasant, exuding a light and unhurried Zen atmosphere able to dissolve the cares of the bustling world. Ascending and gazing about, it seemed as though scenic wonders from every direction had gathered in this one place.
Leaving Deshan Temple, we took a quiet, gentle country road. The rice paddies, just transplanted with seedlings, mirrored the clouds and mountain colors, the whole vast plain a lush green. The village road once traveled by ox carts, the quiet villages, the meandering mountain ridges, the morning mist gradually dispersing... scenes of the old farming village rose unbidden before my eyes: on summer evenings, bare-chested farmers in small groups sitting on wooden benches outside a shop, old villagers puffing on cigarettes and chatting under the shade of trees, farmers shouldering their hoes walking home along the field paths, children carrying schoolbags returning home from school, the occasional bark of a dog echoing down the street... such moving scenes, giving off an air of peace and contentment. "Where the distant mountains meet the setting sun in a haze of mist, it seems as if this is the very place from which I once departed; at the river mouth, village children herd their calves home, and I rein in my horse to ask the way I once came." This poem, 'Mountain Journey,' by the early Qing woman poet Lin Yining, echoes the feeling of that moment.

points.zh: 何充 : 東晉重臣，風韵深沉高雅，以文章德性著稱，言行斗胆特異，獨出形象。終生宏揚佛法，謹守戒律，建立江南第一座尼寺，卽尼姑庵。
賈島 : 唐朝詩人，一生貧寒，早年曾出家爲僧，屢擧進士不第，爲官低下。一生未脫離「僧本位」的思維。其詩作以苦吟為特色，重詞句錘鍊，以幽奇寒僻的風格見長，往往蘊含飄忽的禪思。
points.en: Jia Dao: a Tang dynasty poet who lived a life of poverty; in his early years he became a Buddhist monk, repeatedly failed the imperial examinations, and held only lowly official posts. Throughout his life he never shed a monk's fundamental mindset. His poetry is marked by painstaking composition ('bitter chanting'), a devotion to the meticulous polishing of every phrase, and is noted for its austere, cold, and eccentric style, often carrying a fleeting, Zen-like contemplativeness.
